title: Welcome from the principal
content:
Welcome to St. Martha
Catholic School
Dear St. Martha Families,

Welcome to Saint Martha School! I am grateful that you are part of our school family and
look forward to partnering with you in the year ahead. As we begin this journey together,
our shared mission is to help our students grow as both saints and scholars by weaving our
Catholic faith into every aspect of school life.

This handbook has been prepared to support a successful school year and to help us work
together as a community. The policies and procedures outlined reflect our commitment to
providing a safe, positive, and faith-filled environment where every child can learn, grow,
and thrive.

Please take some time to review the handbook with your child(ren). Keeping the
handbook in a convenient place will make it a helpful resource throughout the school year.

Please sign and date the Parent & Student Handbook Acknowledgment Form
included in your summer packet and return it to school by August 20, 2026.

Thank you for entrusting us with your child's education and faith formation. I am excited
for all that God has in store for our Saint Martha community this year.

Blessings,

Mrs. Amanda Konopaska
Principal
In a loving, nurturing environment, rooted in Jesus Christ, St. Martha Catholic School guides each
student to develop their unique gifts and potential through prayer, study and service.

title: Mission, philosophy & school hours
content:
School Mission Statement

In a loving, nurturing environment, rooted in Jesus Christ, St. Martha Catholic School guides each student to develop their unique gifts and potential through prayer, study and service.

Our Philosophy

We believe the family, as the primary educator, partners with us in the responsibility of preparing students for lifelong journey of faith and learning.
We believe that knowledge of our Catholic beliefs, practices and traditions is critical to students to enable them to develop the moral strength to follow Christ in today’s world.
We believe that Catholic education requires active stewardship rooted in social justice and civic responsibility.
We believe a challenging school wide curriculum rooted in gospel values provides students with optimal opportunities to succeed.
We believe teachers engage in meaningful researched based professional development to improve skills for effective instruction.
We believe students learn best when actively engaged and motivated to become lifelong learners.
We believe in providing differentiated instruction so all students will achieve to their highest potential.

School Hours

Full School Day: 8:00 a.m.-3:25 p.m.
Half School Day: 8:00 a.m.-11:25 a.m.
Preschool & Kindergarten Full Day: 8:00 a.m.-3:20 p.m.
Preschool & Kindergarten Half Day: 8:00 a.m.-11:20 a.m.
Lunch & Recess: 11:30 a.m.-12:20 p.m.
School Office Hours (Monday-Friday): 7:45 a.m.-3:45 p.m.
Before School Care: 7:20 a.m.-7:50 a.m.
After School Care (Kids Corner): 3:25 p.m.-6:00 p.m.

title: Enrollment, admissions & withdrawal
content:
St. Martha School admits students during three consecutive periods to be announced annually in the following order:

January 11, 2027-February 5, 2027
Re-enrollment for current St. Martha School and Preschool students/siblings in good standing under the Tuition Policy.

February 8, 2027-February 19, 2027
For children of the parish.

Beginning on February 22, 2027
For the community at large. If needed, an enrollment waiting list and status will be announced at the conclusion of the period.

Diocesan Policy on the Human Body

Diocesan schools partner with families to educate and form students consistent with the teachings of our Lord, Jesus Christ and His Church, and so families are expected to live in accord with the Gospel values, particularly regarding actions and behaviors that are public. Students and parents (or legal guardians) shall conduct themselves in accord with their God-Given biological sex. Anything to the contrary notwithstanding.

Admissions

Saint Martha School welcomes students of any race, religion, sex, color, national and ethnic origin, to all rights, privileges, programs, and activities generally accorded students at school or made available to students in this school. Every reasonable effort will be made by the St. Martha School staff to meet the academic needs of each student and to help children modify inappropriate student behavior.

St. Martha reserves the right not to enroll, or to request that parents withdraw any student whose academic or behavioral needs cannot be met given the staff, materials, and facilities at St. Martha School.

Withdrawal Policy

• Registration and book fees are nonrefundable.
• Fees for extra-curricular classes (i.e. strings) are nonrefundable.
• Tuition will be refunded according to the following schedule:
• 100% of tuition will be refunded for withdrawals during the 1st through the 5th full day of class.
• 50% of tuition will be refunded for withdrawals during the 6th through 10th full day of class.
• No tuition will be refunded for withdrawals after the 10th full day of class.
subheadings: Diocesan Policy on the Human Body

title: Tuition policy
content:
Tuition rates and fees are established annually by the Pastor and the Parish Finance Council.

Tuition assistance may be available to families who demonstrate a genuine financial need. Families seeking
assistance must submit a Financial Aid application, along with all required supporting financial
documentation, through the FACTS Family Portal by March of the year preceding the upcoming school
year.

In addition to diocesan financial aid, St. Martha School may provide tuition assistance based on available resources.
Once a family's financial need has been assessed, they will be notified and invited to meet with the school’s
accounting team to discuss the level of assistance that may be available.

Tuition and Fee Payments

All families are required to enroll in the FACTS Tuition Management Program upon enrollment or re-
enrollment at St. Martha School. FACTS Family Portal serves as the school's tuition collection system, helping to
ensure the orderly and timely receipt of funds needed to support school operations.

FACTS Family Portal offers several payment plan options, including the ability to spread tuition payments over a
twelve-month period. Families may choose automatic payments from a bank account or credit card. Those who
prefer to pay tuition in full may also do so through the portal. A FACTS enrollment fee of $50 will be applied
by July 1st for all families enrolled in the monthly plan option.

In addition to tuition, charges for lunch accounts, childcare, field trips and other school-related fees will be billed
and collected through the FACTS Family Portal.

If a special need arises during the year due to unforeseen circumstances, immediate contact should be made with
the principal to address the solution ofthe tuition payment. The situation will remain confidential and can be readily
resolved through the parents' initiative.

RaiseRight Program (Tuition Credit)

The St. Martha RaiseRight Program provides families with an easy way to reduce tuition costs through everyday
purchases. Families purchase gift cards at their full face value from participating retailers, restaurants, gas stations,
and other businesses they regularly use. For example, a $100 gift card costs $100.

When gift cards are purchased through Raise Right, the participating vendor provides a rebate based on a
percentage of the card's value. The rebate amount varies by retailer. St. Martha School tracks the rebates earned by
each family and returns 90% of the accumulated rebate to the family as a tuition credit. The remaining 10% is
retained to offset administrative expenses such as shipping and bank fees.

Unlike some schools that use gift card programs primarily as fundraisers, the Raise Right Program at St. Martha is
designed to directly benefit participating families by helping reduce tuition costs. Families may choose to have their
earned credits applied to tuition on either a quarterly or annual basis.
For additional information about the Raise Right Program, please refer to the resource linked below.

RaiseRight Program Information
To ensure continued enrollment, all tuition and fee accounts must be current at the end of each semester. Families
with outstanding balances will not be permitted to re-enroll for the following school year until their account has
been brought into good standing.

title: Attendance & reporting an absence
content:
Regular attendance is essential for a child's social, emotional, and academic
development. Establishing a consistent routine helps children build a sense of
structure and responsibility while making the most of their experience.
Below are our policies regarding attendance, absences, and tardiness.

The Michigan School Code states that parents or guardians are responsible for ensuring that children between
the ages of six and sixteen attend school regularly. Consistent attendance is essential for academic success and
allows students to fully benefit from classroom instruction. Students are expected to attend school regularly
and arrive on time each day. Punctuality and attendance help students develop habits of responsibility, self-
discipline, and respect for the learning environment.

Regular student attendance is a shared responsibility between home and school. This partnership plays a vital
role in promoting positive attendance habits and supporting student achievement.

Parents are strongly encouraged to schedule family vacations during designated school breaks and
vacation periods whenever possible. While regular attendance is expected, some absences are unavoidable.

Absences due to personal illness, a death in the family, or medical appointments that cannot be scheduled
outside of school hours are considered understandable and appropriate reasons for missing school.

In accordance with Michigan law:

A student is considered chronically absent when they miss 10% or more of the enrolled school days
during a school year.
A student is considered truant when they accumulate ten (10) or more unexcused absences during a school
year. Once a student is identified as truant, attendance will be monitored throughout the remainder of the
school year until consistent improvement is demonstrated.
Cases involving chronic absenteeism or truancy may be referred to the Ingham County Truancy
Coordinator for additional support and intervention.

Reporting an Absence or Early Dismissal

If your child will be absent, please notify the school by calling (517) 349-3322 or by emailing both your
child's teacher and the school secretary no later than 8:00 a.m. on the day of the absence.

If a student needs to leave school before the end of the day, a parent or guardian should email the teacher and
school secretary with the reason for the early dismissal. The student must be signed out in the school office by
an authorized adult before leaving the building. Upon pickup, any adult other than the child's parent(s) must
present a valid photo ID before the child will be released. When returning to school, the student must check in
at the school office before returning to class. For the safety of our students, children will only be released to
individuals listed on the student's authorized pick-up form.
subheadings: Reporting an Absence or Early Dismissal

title: Tardiness
content:
Arriving at school on time is essential for student success. Punctuality allows students to fully benefit from
classroom instruction while developing habits of responsibility, self-discipline, and respect for others. Because
learning begins promptly each day, families are expected to make every effort to ensure that students arrive on
time.

Tardiness not only affects the late student but also disrupts the learning environment for the entire class.
When students arrive after the school day has begun, teachers must interrupt instruction to update attendance
and lunch counts, and the movement of students entering classrooms can distract both teachers and
classmates. While occasional tardiness may be unavoidable, repeated tardiness is a cause for concern and may
require school intervention.

Students may enter the building beginning at 7:50 a.m.
Any student who is not in the classroom by 8:00 a.m. will be marked tardy.

On Thursdays, students arriving between 8:20 a.m. and 9:15 a.m. will not be admitted into the school
building until Mass has concluded. Please plan arrival times accordingly.

If you know your child will be arriving late, please notify the school by calling the office or emailing both the
teacher and school secretary. If your child will be purchasing a school lunch, please include that information
in your communication. When excessive tardiness occurs, the teacher will contact the family to express
concern and discuss ways to improve attendance. If necessary, a meeting may be scheduled to develop a plan
for consistent, on-time arrival.

Parents and guardians are respectfully asked not to accompany tardy students to the classroom, as doing so
may further disrupt instruction. Students should report to the school office upon arrival and follow the
established sign-in procedures. Please remember that students depend on their parents and guardians to help
them arrive at school on time each day.

For attendance purposes, students who arrive after 10:00 a.m. or leave before 1:00 p.m. will be
considered absent for one-half day.

title: Uniform, dress code & spirit wear
content:
(See Uniform Booklet for complete uniform requirements.)

St. Martha School is a Catholic school and reserves the right to establish and enforce a uniform dress code for all
students. Proper school attire and good grooming contribute to a positive learning environment and support
students' educational, social, and spiritual development. Our uniform policy reflects Christian values of modesty,

respect, and dignity, emphasizing that our students are valued for who they are rather than what they wear.
Uniforms also promote school unity, school pride, and minimize distractions in the learning environment.

School Uniforms

Official St. Martha School uniforms must be purchased through My APlus Uniforms (MAPU) and will feature
the St. Martha School logo. To ensure consistency, all required uniform items must be purchased directly
through MAPU. Alternative brands or substitute uniform pieces are not permitted. Families are
encouraged to order uniforms well in advance to allow adequate time for processing and delivery.
Students should arrive at school each day in clean, properly fitting uniforms.

Cold Weather

Coats, jackets, blankets, and non-uniform sweatshirts may not be worn inside the school building. Students who
become cold should wear the approved St. Martha uniform sweater as outlined in the Uniform Booklet.

Non-Uniform (Free Dress) Days

Unless otherwise announced, all scheduled half days are designated as non-uniform days.
Students may wear modest, school-appropriate clothing that reflects Christian values and is suitable for the
educational environment.

Acceptable Attire

Shorts must be school-appropriate in length, providing appropriate coverage and maintaining a neat, modest
appearance. Shorts may only be worn August-October and after Spring Break only. The principal reserves
the right to determine whether clothing meets the school's dress code expectations.
Capris, skirts, dresses, skorts, or shorts that meet the fingertip length requirement.
Comfortable, closed-toe or secure footwear appropriate for school activities.

The Following Are Not Permitted

Pajamas or slippers
Tank tops, spaghetti straps, crop tops, or strapless tops
Clothing that is excessively tight or revealing
Clothing with inappropriate language, images, political endorsements, or controversial messages
Hats or hoods worn inside the building
Flip-flops, high heels, or loose-fitting sandals
If there is any question regarding the appropriateness of an item, families should contact the school office
before it is worn to school.

Birthday Free Dress

Students may enjoy a free dress day on their birthday. If a birthday falls on a weekend, holiday, all school photo
or other day when school is not in session, the classroom teacher will designate an alternate free dress day.

St. Martha Spirit Wear Days

Spirit Wear Days are opportunities to celebrate our school community while maintaining a neat and appropriate
appearance. If you choose not to wear spirit wear, uniforms are required.

Students may wear:

Official St. Martha Spirit Wear purchased from Fabricated Customs
https://fabricatedcustoms.com/collections/school-apparel-shop-for-st-martha-miracles
Approved Mileage Club and school fundraiser shirts
Catholic School League jerseys when specifically permitted.

Spirit Wear may be worn with:

Jeans in good condition
Athletic or uniform shorts (during approved months)
Track pants, skirts, skorts, or other approved bottoms
Athletic or regular shoes with socks must be worn. CROCS are not permitted.

On scheduled game or meet days, student-athletes participating in Jr. Cougar athletics or other Catholic league
sports may wear their team uniform top with approved uniform bottoms. Sleeveless athletic jerseys must be worn
over a T-shirt.

Click to access our online Spirit Wear Shop!

General Appearance Guidelines

Students are expected to maintain a neat, clean, and modest appearance.
Hair should be clean, neatly groomed, and kept out of the eyes.
Jewelry should be minimal.
Girls may wear one pair of small stud earrings. Hoop earrings, dangling earrings and bracelets are not
permitted.
Small cross necklaces or religious medals may be worn.
Students in Grades 3–8 may wear a plain watch or basic fitness/activity tracker.

Smart watches are not permitted and must be turned into the teacher if brought to school. They
can be picked up by a parent at dismissal.
Watches are not permitted in Kindergarten through Grade 2.

Nails and Makeup

Nail polish on natural nails is permitted.
Artificial nails, acrylic nails, gel extensions, or similar enhancements are not permitted.
Makeup is not permitted.

Accessories

Purses and unnecessary accessories should remain at home unless specifically requested by the school.

Uniform Policy Enforcement

Parental support of the St. Martha Uniform and Dress Code is greatly appreciated. Families are encouraged to
help students make appropriate clothing choices before arriving at school.
Students who are not dressed according to the Uniform and Dress Code may be required to:

Change into clothing from the school's Care Closet, or
Have appropriate clothing brought from home.
Repeated violations of the Uniform and Dress Code may result in disciplinary action.

Warm Weather Uniform

The warm weather uniform, including approved uniform shorts, may be worn only during August, September,
October and after Spring Break. (typically April, May, and June)
At all other times, students are expected to wear the standard uniform as outlined in the Uniform Booklet.

General Uniform Expectations

Shirts must remain tucked in at all times.

Belts are required whenever pants or shorts include belt loops.
Shorts are designated for the spring and summer uniform season.
Winter uniform sweaters, vests, and cardigans should be worn as designated.
Shoes should be clean, safe, and appropriate for school activities.

Shoes with lights, excessive colors, wheels, or distracting features are not permitted.
Uniform items designated as required must be purchased through MAPU.

title: Academic policies
content:
Homework

Homework is an important part of the learning process. It reinforces and extends what students learn in class
while also helping to build strong study habits and personal responsibility. In many cases, homework consists of
work that was not completed during the school day. Students are expected to complete and return all assignments
by the designated due date. Homework may include daily reading, math fact practice, studying for assessments, or
other assignments that support classroom learning.

Recommended home study times vary by grade level. Please note that middle school assignments requiring
printing must be completed at home, as teachers and the school office are not able to print homework. This
expectation supports student organization, responsibility, and preparation for the expectations of high school.

Make-Up Work

Time away from school for travel or vacations is strongly discouraged, as students miss important classroom
instruction that cannot be fully made up. If an absence for travel is necessary, families should notify the teacher
in advance. While teachers may not be able to provide work ahead of time, students may be allowed to take
books or copies of materials to keep up with regularly assigned work. Teachers will determine which assignments
must be completed, and any worksheets missed during the absence will be provided upon return. It is the
responsibility of the student and family to complete and submit all assigned work and to arrange any missed
assessments with the teacher.

Middle School (5th-8th) Late & Missing Work Policy

Late assignments receive an automatic 10% deduction from the earned score. Missing assignments will be
marked with an 'M' in the gradebook, which calculates as a 0% until submitted. Late work is subject to a strict
time limit and will not be accepted if more than 10 days late unless approved by the teacher.

Parent/Teacher Conferences

Parent/Teacher Conferences will be held twice a year for Preschool – 8th Grade.
Both the Fall and Spring Parent-Teacher Conferences are required. Additional conferences may be requested by a
teacher or parent as needed. Parents are encouraged to maintain regular communication with their child’s
teacher(s). For students in grades 4–8, parents are encouraged to regularly access the FACTS Family Portal to
monitor academic progress.

Report Cards

Report cards are issued four times a year, at the end of each quarter, in grades K-8. They will be emailed and
posted on FACTS Family Portal to review them. You may print or save to keep a long-term copy. After 2 weeks,
report cards will be archived and no longer available to view through FACTS Family Portal. Should you need
access after this time, please contact the school office.

NWEA Assessments

NWEA assessments are administered three times each year, in the Fall, Winter, and Spring for students in grades
2–8. These diagnostic tests help identify individual student strengths and areas for growth, while also tracking
academic progress over time. Specific testing dates will be shared in the News Notes.

title: School policies
content:
Birthdays & Celebrations

Parents wishing to celebrate their child's birthday at school should first check with the classroom teacher. We
encourage simple celebrations and ask families to consider healthy treats, individually packaged snacks or non-
food alternatives such as pencils, stickers, bookmarks, or other small trinkets. Please be mindful of classroom
allergy restrictions and do not send nut products to nut-restricted classrooms.

Party invitations may be distributed at school only if the entire class, all boys, or all girls are invited. When
invitations are limited to a smaller group, families are asked to distribute them outside of school and encourage
discretion to avoid hurt feelings. Please do not have balloons, flowers, gifts, or other celebratory items delivered
to school. Any items delivered will remain in the office until the end of the school day.
Students may enjoy a free dress day on their birthday. If a birthday falls on a non-school day, the teacher will
work with the student to select an alternate day for birthday free dress.

Building Access
For the safety and security of our students and staff, all school entrance doors and parish access doors are locked
each school day at 8:05 a.m.. Anyone arriving after that time must enter through the main school entrance and
use the doorbell to gain access and check in at the office.

Recess

Recess and free play are important parts of a child's development, providing opportunities for physical activity,
social interaction, and fresh air. Students are provided a recess period each day and will go outside whenever
weather conditions permit. Students will participate in outdoor recess when the actual temperature or wind chill
is 10°F or above. Families should ensure that children come to school dressed appropriately for the weather.

During the winter months, this includes warm coats, hats, gloves, boots, and snow pants when necessary.

A written note from a physician is required for a student to be excused from outdoor recess for medical reasons.

Sports & Athletics

St. Martha School values athletic opportunities and relies on parent volunteers to organize and coach
extracurricular sports programs. Coaches, athletes, and spectators are expected to model Christ-like
sportsmanship at all times. Students must attend school on the day of a practice or game in order to participate
in that activity. Any team apparel or spirit wear featuring the St. Martha logo must receive approval from the
principal before being produced.

Visitors

St. Martha School welcomes visitors and values family involvement. To ensure a positive learning environment,
all visits should be arranged in advance with the teacher and principal. For the safety and security of students and
staff, all visitors and volunteers must register in the school office upon arrival and receive a visitors badge. To
minimize classroom interruptions, parents are asked to leave forgotten items clearly labeled in the school office
rather than delivering them directly to classrooms.
Parents are also welcome to attend morning prayer and Mass. If joining, please park in the south lot and enter
through the church entrance after student drop-off.

Volunteers

Volunteer support is an essential part of the St. Martha School community. Each family is asked to contribute a
minimum of 20 volunteer hours per school year, while preschool and single-parent families are asked to
contribute a minimum of 10 hours. Volunteer opportunities will be communicated throughout the school year.
Families are encouraged to participate and should complete any required forms or documentation as requested.

All volunteer hours must be recorded by each family directly in the FACTS Family Portal. Periodic
reports may be provided to families who are not meeting the required hours. This expectation is part of our
school covenant and helps support the overall operation of the school in keeping tuition costs accessible.

For the safety and learning environment of our students, volunteers are asked not to bring infants or
preschool-aged children while serving in the school.

All volunteers working with students, including classroom support, coaching, and field trips, must complete the
Diocese of Lansing Virtus “Protecting God’s Children” training. Background checks are also required, and
fingerprinting may be necessary for individuals who have not resided in Michigan for the past 10 years and will
be volunteering with students.
For security purposes, all volunteers must sign in at the school office upon arrival and wear a visitor
badge while in the building.

Parking for Volunteers
To help ensure student safety, parent volunteers who are working in the building between 8:15 a.m. and 3:15 p.m.
are asked to park in the south parking lot near the church entrance. The north parking lot, adjacent to the school
entrance, should remain free of parked vehicles during the school day to provide a safer route for students
traveling to and from the playground.

Weapons Policy: Public Act 250 of 1995
In accordance with Section 1311 of the Michigan School Code (MCL 380.1311), schools are required to expel
any student who possesses a dangerous weapon in a weapon-free school zone, school building, or on school
grounds. This provision became effective December 29, 1995.

title: Weekly school liturgy
content:
The Eucharistic Liturgy and religious education are the foundation of our values-based Catholic education. An all-
school Mass is celebrated each Thursday at 8:20 a.m., with students actively helping to prepare the
liturgy. In addition, Grades 4–8 attend Mass on Mondays at 8:20 a.m., and Grades K–3 attend Mass on Fridays at
8:20 a.m. On Mass days, church doors are locked beginning at 8:30 a.m.

Parents are warmly welcome to attend student Masses. If attending, please park in the south parking lot near the
church entrance and enter and exit through those doors, as school doors are locked after morning drop-off.

title: Family involvement & volunteering
content:
At St. Martha School, we believe that education is a shared mission between home, school, and parish. Our
students thrive when families and staff work together in partnership to support faith formation, academic growth,
and community life.

Family involvement is an essential part of who we are as a Catholic school. Every family has unique gifts, talents,

and time to offer, and we are committed to providing meaningful opportunities for all families to participate in the
life of our school.

Rather than operating as a traditional parent organization, St. Martha School embraces a model of shared
responsibility and open participation. This structure is designed to ensure that volunteer opportunities are
accessible, clearly communicated, and equitably shared across our school community.

Family involvement is coordinated through a simple and transparent system that includes a School Liaison,
Classroom Liaisons, and a community of parent volunteers. This approach allows families to engage in ways that
best fit their availability and interests while ensuring that school events and activities are well supported.

Our guiding belief is simple:
Every family has gifts to share, and every contribution strengthens our community.

*NEW* Family Involvement Structure
Family involvement at St. Martha School is organized through a simple and transparent structure designed to make
participation accessible to all families. Rather than relying on a formal organization or limited group of volunteers,
opportunities are shared broadly so that any family may choose to participate based on interest, availability, and
gifts.

Coordination is supported through a School Liaison, who serves as the main point of communication and
organization, Classroom Liaisons who help share information and connect families within each classroom, and
Event Coordinators who may assist with specific school events as needed. All families are considered part of the
volunteer community and are invited to participate through open sign-ups and shared opportunities throughout the
year.

This structure ensures that involvement remains welcoming, equitable, and centered on building a strong school
community together.

Guiding Principles

Family involvement at St. Martha School is built on the following beliefs:
Every family has gifts to share.
Volunteer opportunities should be open and accessible to all.
Responsibilities should be shared rather than concentrated among a few individuals.

Participation strengthens relationships and builds community.
We are partners in supporting the mission of St. Martha School and helping students grow in faith,
knowledge, and virtue.

Classroom Liaisons (Preschool-8th Grade)

Each classroom will have one teacher selected Classroom Liaison.
The Classroom Liaison serves as a bridge between families, the classroom teacher, and the School Liaison.

Responsibilities

Welcome new families
Share volunteer opportunities with classroom families
Help recruit volunteers when needed
Assist with classroom celebrations and teacher appreciation efforts
Encourage participation from all families
Communicate classroom needs to the School Liaison
Classroom Liaisons are not event planners or decision-makers. Their primary role is communication,

hospitality, and volunteer recruitment. Parents serving as Classroom Liaisons are expected to attend a
beginning-of-the-year training to review the responsibilities and expectations of the role. Volunteer hours for
the Classroom Liaison position will be credited for this role.

Event Coordinators

For larger school events, parent volunteers may serve as Event Coordinators.
Examples may include:

Daddy-Daughter Dance
Mother-Son Event
Catholic Schools Week
Teacher Appreciation Week

Responsibilities

Work with the School Liaison to plan the event
Recruit volunteers in connection with the Classroom Liaisons
Delegate responsibilities
Coordinate event logistics
Support successful implementation
Event Coordinators are appointed through the principal and school liaison on an event-by-event basis and are
not permanent positions.

Volunteer Community

All families are considered part of the Volunteer Community.
At the beginning of each school year, families will complete a Volunteer Interest Form indicating:
Areas of interest
Skills and talents
Availability
Interest in serving as an Event Coordinator
Volunteer opportunities are then shared through News Notes, email, or Sign-Up Genius so that all families
have the opportunity to participate. This process ensures that involvement is communicated openly and
remains accessible to all families.

title: Field trips & class trips
content:
Field trips are an important extension of the curriculum and are considered required instructional time.
Parents will be notified in advance of scheduled trips and will receive detailed information along with fees and

All field trips are typically held within a 100-mile radius unless prior approval is granted by the principal.

title: Health & wellness
content:
Food Allergies, Intolerances & Nut Restrictions

Parents are responsible for notifying both the school office and the classroom teacher of any food allergies or
intolerances so that appropriate precautions can be taken to maintain a safe environment for all students. Some
classrooms may be designated as nut-restricted when a student with a diagnosed allergy is enrolled. Students may
still bring nut-containing foods in their lunches; however, they will be asked to sit in a designated area to help
reduce the risk of cross-contact.

To support student safety, children should not share food, and students who consume nut products should wash
their hands afterward. While every effort is made to reduce risk, a completely allergen-free environment cannot be
guaranteed. Families are encouraged to educate their children about their individual health needs and how to
manage them at school.

EpiPen Policy for Students with Severe Allergies

If your child has a life-threatening allergy that may require an EpiPen, it is essential that the school is fully
informed. Parents must provide a current physician-signed Allergy Action Plan, at least one (preferably
two) labeled and unexpired EpiPens to be kept at school, and clear instructions for when and how the
medication should be administered.

EpiPens are stored in a secure but accessible location, and staff are trained in their use. If a student is approved by
their physician and parent to carry their own EpiPen, appropriate documentation must be on file in the school
office. While every effort is made to reduce risk, a completely allergen-free environment cannot be guaranteed.

Open communication and partnership between home and school are essential in supporting the safety of students
with severe allergies.

Injuries at School

Every precaution is taken to provide a safe environment for students. If a minor injury occurs, basic first aid will be
provided, such as cleaning and bandaging cuts or applying ice to bumps.
In the case of a serious injury, emergency procedures will be followed and parents will be notified as soon as the
student is stable and appropriate care has been provided.

Illness

Children should not be sent to school when they are ill. Students should remain at home if they:
• are too ill to go outside
• show signs of a significant cold or require medication such as cough syrup or antihistamines
• have an elevated temperature or fever
• have been on antibiotics for fewer than 24 hours
• have vomited or have had diarrhea within the past 24 hours
• have unexplained or untreated skin rashes or lesions
A physician’s note is required for a student to remain inside during recess due to illness.
Parents are asked to notify the school office promptly of any communicable diseases, as these must be reported to
the health department. If a student becomes ill during the school day, they will be isolated and made comfortable
while parents are contacted for pick-up. Families should ensure they are reachable during school hours and that
voicemail is available. If parents cannot be reached in a timely manner, emergency contacts listed on file will be
contacted.

Immunizations

Michigan law requires that children be fully immunized prior to entering school for the first time. Parents must
provide a current certificate of immunization from a physician or submit a signed waiver no later than the first day
of school. An updated immunization certificate is also required prior to a student entering 7th grade. 27
Medications
Medications should be administered at home whenever possible. If medication must be given during the
school day, parents must complete a medication authorization form with specific instructions.
All prescription medications must be delivered to the school office by a parent in the original labeled container,
clearly showing the student’s name, physician’s name, medication name and strength, and dosage instructions.
The use of non-prescription medications, including cough drops, is strongly discouraged.

Supporting Student Mental Health and Safety

At St. Martha School, we are committed to supporting the emotional and mental well-being of all students. We
recognize that students may experience anxiety, depression, or other forms of emotional distress, and we take all
concerns seriously, including any expression or threat of harm to self or others.

Our first priority is safety. If a student is in crisis or makes any statement related to self-harm or harm to others,
they are never left alone, and administration is notified immediately. All threats whether verbal, written, or implied
are taken seriously. Parents are contacted as soon as possible, and the student may be sent home for further
evaluation. In cases of active suicidal ideation, intent, plan, or behavior, emergency medical evaluation is
appropriate. Any targeted threat of violence will be reviewed by the school BTAM team in coordination with local
law enforcement.

We approach mental health concerns as health matters, not disciplinary issues, and work to support students
through communication with families and referrals to outside professionals. In some situations, a student may be
asked to remain home temporarily while a safety plan is developed. A re-entry meeting and a physician’s note may
be required before returning to school.

Our staff receives ongoing training to recognize signs of emotional distress, and students are provided with age-
appropriate tools to help them identify and express their feelings and seek help when needed. We encourage open
partnership with families. If a student is struggling emotionally, school personnel will communicate concerns to
parents, and we also encourage parents to reach out proactively with any concerns. Together, we can ensure
students receive the support they need to thrive academically, emotionally, and spiritually.

Community Mental Health Resources
If you are concerned about your child’s mental health, the following organizations may be helpful:
CEI-CMH Families Forward (517) 346-8200; Access Center (517)346-8318
Michigan State University Outpatient Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Clinic: 517-353-3070
Mid-Mitten Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (Samantha Kennedy, DO): 517-347-8420
University of Michigan Outpatient Psychiatric Services: 734-764-0231
Pine Rest Christian Mental Health Services: 616-455-5000
Parents may reach out to P2P if additional guidance is needed with respect to obtaining psychiatric services or
if access to care questions arise. (www.prevent2protect.msu.edu)

Pesticides

As part of St. Martha School’s pest management program, pesticides may be applied on an occasional basis.
Families have the right to be informed of any pesticide applications made to school grounds or buildings. If you
wish to receive notification of pesticide use, please contact the school office.

title: Bullying information
content:
At St. Martha School, every student has the right to learn in a safe, respectful, and Christ-centered environment.

Bullying, harassment, intimidation, and other behaviors that interfere with a student's well-being or ability to learn
are not tolerated.

Bullying is defined as repeated, intentional behavior that causes physical, emotional, social, or
psychological harm and involves an imbalance of power. Bullying may occur in person, in writing,
electronically, or through social media. Examples include:
Physical aggression or threats of harm
Name-calling, insults, or hurtful comments
Spreading rumors or sharing secrets
Purposeful exclusion from peer groups or activities
Inappropriate or offensive comments
Harassing messages through text, email, social media, or other electronic means

Bullying vs. Conflict

It is important to distinguish bullying from normal conflict. Conflict occurs when two or more individuals disagree
or have different perspectives, needs, or goals. Conflict is a normal part of life and can often be resolved through
communication, problem-solving, and reconciliation. Bullying, however, is intentional, repeated, and involves one
person or group using power to harm, intimidate, or control another person.

Examples of Prohibited Behavior

The following behaviors may be considered bullying, harassment, or other serious misconduct:

Physical Aggression
Hitting, striking, kicking, pushing, tripping, or other actions intended to cause harm
Verbal or Emotional Harassment
Name-calling, insults, teasing intended to hurt, threats, intimidation, or humiliation
Social Exclusion
Deliberately excluding others, encouraging others not to be friends with someone, or spreading rumors
Cyberbullying
Sending threatening or hurtful messages
Posting insulting comments online
Creating fake accounts to deceive or embarrass others
Sharing photos, videos, or personal information without permission

Reporting and Investigation

All reports of bullying or serious misconduct will be taken seriously. When incidents are reported but not directly
witnessed by a staff member, the school will conduct an investigation and gather information from those involved.
Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.

Our Commitment

Discipline at St. Martha School is guided by compassion, fairness, and a commitment to helping students grow in
virtue. While consequences may be necessary, our ultimate goal is to form students who treat others with dignity,
respect, and Christ-like love.
subheadings: Bullying is defined as repeated, intentional behavior that causes physical, emotional, social, or psychological harm and involves an imbalance of power.

title: Sexual harassment
content:
St. Martha Catholic School is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and Christ-centered environment for
all students, staff, and members of the school community. Sexual harassment of any kind is prohibited and will
not be tolerated.

Sexual harassment may include, but is not limited to:

Verbal Harassment

Sexual comments, jokes, or innuendos
Suggestive remarks or propositions
Written messages of a sexual nature
Sexual threats directed toward a student, staff member, or other member of the school community

Nonverbal Harassment

Displaying sexually suggestive objects, pictures, or written materials
Inappropriate gestures, sounds, leering, whistling, or other actions of a sexual nature
Any nonverbal behavior intended to demean, intimidate, or offend another person

Physical Harassment

Unwanted touching or physical contact of a sexual nature
Attempts to engage in unwanted physical contact
Pinching, grabbing, pushing, or other inappropriate physical interactions directed toward a student, staff
member, or other member of the school community

Consequences

Any report of sexual harassment will be investigated promptly and appropriately by school administration.

Depending on the nature, severity, and circumstances of the incident, disciplinary action may include, but is
not limited to:
Verbal warning
Documentation of the incident
Notification of parent(s)/guardian(s)
Conference with the student, parent(s)/guardian(s), principal, and/or pastor
Suspension from school
Behavioral or disciplinary conditions for continued enrollment
Expulsion
Disciplinary consequences will be determined by the principal and pastor based on the severity, frequency, and
circumstances of the behavior.

St. Martha School reserves the right to impose more serious consequences for severe incidents, even
on a first offense, when necessary to protect the safety and well-being of students and staff.

title: Emergency procedures & safety guidelines
content:
Fire and Tornado Drills

In accordance with Michigan law, students regularly practice fire and emergency drills to ensure they can exit the
building quickly and safely.

In the event of a tornado watch, weather conditions will be closely monitored and staff will be alerted to prepare
students to take appropriate shelter. If a tornado warning is issued, students will remain in designated safe areas
until an all-clear signal is given. If severe weather occurs, parents may choose to pick up their children as safety
conditions allow.

Lockdown Drills

Lockdown drills are conducted in accordance with Michigan law to ensure that students and staff are prepared to
respond quickly and safely in the event of a dangerous or threatening situation. The purpose of a lockdown is to
secure the school building and protect all occupants during an emergency.

Students and staff will practice lockdown procedures as required. At the start of the school year, drills will be
scheduled and families will be notified in advance through News Notes. During a lockdown, no one, including
students, staff, or parents are permitted to enter or exit the building until the all-clear is given.

School Closing

In the event of school closure due to inclement weather or other emergency conditions, local television stations
will be notified. Families will also receive immediate notification via email and text messaging, and announcements
will be posted on the school’s Facebook page.

If school must close during the school day, parents are asked to pick up their children as soon as possible. If a
parent is unable to do so, arrangements should be made for the child to go home with a friend or approved
emergency contact. If students are not picked up within a reasonable time, individuals listed on the emergency
contact card will be notified.

Hazardous Travel Conditions

Students travel to school from a wide range of locations where weather conditions may vary. Even when St. Martha
School is open, parents who feel that travel is unsafe should keep their child home until conditions improve and
notify the school office of the absence. If weather or road conditions become dangerous during the school day,
parents who are concerned may pick up their child at their discretion.

School Crisis Plan

St. Martha School maintains a comprehensive crisis plan developed in partnership with Meridian Township Police
and Fire Departments to address a range of emergencies, including fire, medical incidents, accidents, and biological,

radiological, chemical, or other security threats.

In accordance with Diocesan policy, the school may implement a lockdown or lockout procedure during periods of
heightened alert. Staff are trained in these procedures, and the building is equipped with interior and exterior
security cameras. During such events, all exterior doors will remain locked.

Families will be notified as quickly as possible through email and text messaging. In an emergency, families are
asked to keep phone lines open so school staff can communicate effectively with emergency responders
and authorities.

Asbestos Hazard Emergency Response Act (AHERA)

In compliance with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Asbestos Hazard Emergency
Response Act (AHERA), St. Martha School conducted inspections of all school buildings for asbestos-containing
materials in 1990. The inspection results and asbestos management plans have been maintained on file in the
school administrative office since that time.

In accordance with EPA requirements, asbestos inspections are conducted every three years to ensure ongoing
safety and compliance.

Child Protection Law

All school personnel have completed Virtus training, as well as required fingerprinting and background checks, to
help ensure a safe environment for students.

In accordance with state law, all school and parish employees are mandated reporters and must immediately report
any suspected child abuse or neglect involving a student under the age of 18 to the appropriate authorities. The
Chairperson of the Diocesan Department of Education and Catechesis will also be notified in writing of any such
report.

title: Lunch program
content:
Lansing Catholic High School provides St. Martha School with a catered hot lunch and milk service on most school
days. A monthly menu is provided by Lansing Catholic and shared in News Notes. Lunch selections must be
submitted by the 20th of the preceding month for the entire following month's lunch orders. This advance
deadline ensures adequate time for planning, ordering, and meal preparation.

The lunch program is managed through your FACTS Family Portal. Each family maintains one account for all
children, and no lunch tickets are required. Families will receive an automated notification when their balance falls
to $10.00 or below.

Lunches from Home

Students bringing lunch from home should bring items that do not require refrigeration or freezer storage, as
school refrigerators and freezers are not available for student use. Fast food, restaurant food, and soda are not
permitted. The school office does not accept food deliveries of any kind.

If a student cannot consume the milk provided with hot lunch, they should bring a water bottle instead. Students
with nut-containing lunches will be seated in a designated area to reduce the risk of cross-contact. Families are
asked to avoid sending food in glass containers.

Microwaves

Students in grades 4–8 may use microwaves to heat lunch items that require less than three minutes to warm.
Microwave use is limited to simple reheating; full microwave meals (e.g., frozen dinners or boxed pasta meals) are
not permitted. Foods containing peanuts or nuts may not be heated in the microwave.

Students in grades K–3 are not permitted to use microwaves and should not bring foods that require heating.

title: Student academic & behavior concerns
content:
When an incident or concern arises during the school day, the teacher will reach out to families if they feel it is
necessary. Our approach is rooted in building a strong community of relationships, where situations are addressed
with integrity, care, and love. Most concerns are handled directly between teacher and student through respectful
dialogue that allows students to learn and grow from the experience.

St. Martha School is called to be set apart and to love one another as God loves us. We welcome parent
engagement and recognize that a strong home–school partnership is essential to student success. When concerns
arise, we follow a process modeled after Matthew 18:15–17:
If your child shares a concern from school, we ask that you:
Ask questions to gain a full understanding of the situation.
Stay calm and assume positive intent.
Keep concerns within your family.
Contact the teacher or staff member directly in a respectful and collaborative manner.
Be open to the teacher gathering additional information before responding.
Review and discuss the teacher’s response with your child.

Follow up with the teacher if there are remaining questions or concerns.
If needed, a parent–teacher–student conference may be arranged.
Principal Involvement
If the concern remains unresolved after genuine collaboration with the teacher or staff member, it should
be brought to the principal with all parties involved.
Pastoral Involvement
If the concern is still not resolved after working with the principal, it may then be brought to the pastor.

If a concern is brought directly to the principal, you will be asked to first discuss the matter with the
appropriate teacher or staff member before administrative involvement.

Faculty and staff will not share information regarding another student, including disciplinary consequences. This
protects student privacy and reflects our commitment to forming children in virtue and supporting their growth as
Catholic Christian disciples. This process is intended to foster transparency, respect, and healthy communication
within our school community.

title: Discipline philosophy & Education in Virtue
content:
At St. Martha Catholic School, we are committed to forming students in Gospel values and virtue so they may live
as reflections of Christ. Our mission is to provide a Christ-centered, safe, and nurturing learning environment
grounded in the teachings of the Catholic Church.

We believe discipline is an opportunity for formation rather than punishment. Our goal is to help students develop
self-control, moral awareness, and an understanding of how their choices affect themselves and others. Every
member of our staff shares the responsibility of guiding students with consistency, compassion, and respect,
helping them grow academically, socially, emotionally, and spiritually.

Whenever possible, logical consequences are our first response to student behavior. Logical consequences help
students recognize the connection between their choices and the outcomes of those choices, encouraging
responsibility, accountability, and growth. Rather than asking, "How do we punish this behavior?" we ask, "What
can this student learn from this experience?"

Logical consequences are:

Related to the behavior.

Respectful of the dignity of every student.
Reasonable and intended to teach rather than punish.

Depending on the situation, logical consequences may include taking a break to regain self-control, repairing or
cleaning up a problem that was created, temporarily losing a privilege that was misused, or practicing the expected
behavior correctly. While logical consequences are our primary approach, additional interventions or disciplinary
action may be necessary when behaviors are repeated, significantly disrupt learning, or compromise the safety or
well-being of others.

In all disciplinary situations, the following principles guide our decisions:
Students learn that every choice has a consequence.

Teachers use their professional judgment to maintain a safe, respectful, and orderly learning environment, and
their authority is to be respected.
Decisions are made with the best interest of both the individual student and the entire school community in
mind.
Every interaction is an opportunity to teach, restore relationships, and help students grow in virtue.

Respectful behavior is rooted in keeping Christ at the center of our actions. We expect students to demonstrate
kindness, honesty, responsibility, courtesy, and consideration for others while honoring the expectations of home,
school, and community.

Education in Virtue

St. Martha School implements the Education in Virtue program developed by the Dominican Sisters of Mary. This
program provides a clear and practical framework for helping students develop the habits of virtue as a way of life.

Students grow in virtue through three intentional stages:
Learn – Students are taught what each virtue is and how it is lived in everyday life.
Live – Students intentionally practice virtuous habits through their words, choices, and actions.
Witness – As virtue becomes a habit, students deepen their friendship with Christ and naturally choose what is
good with greater freedom, confidence, and joy.
By partnering with families and embracing virtue formation throughout the school day, we strive to develop not
only successful learners, but faithful disciples who seek to know, love, and serve Christ in all they do.

title: Student behavior expectations
content:
The following expectations apply to all students during the school day, Kids Corner, and any school or parish-
sponsored events. These guidelines help maintain a safe, respectful, and Christ-centered learning environment.

1.Students are expected to be respectful, responsible, and ready to learn each day. This includes arriving to class
on time, following directions, and actively participating in learning.

2.Students are expected to complete all classwork and homework honestly and submit it by the assigned due
date. Academic integrity is essential; cheating, plagiarism, copying others’ work, or inappropriate use of artificial
intelligence is not permitted.
3.Students are expected to follow the school dress code and uniform policy throughout the school day.
4.Personal items that are not related to school learning should remain at home. This includes toys, games, smart
watches, electronic devices, and similar items.
5.Cell phones brought to school must be turned in to the classroom teacher at the start of the day and will be
returned at dismissal. Misuse of this expectation may result in the phone being held in the office for parent
pickup.
6.Gum chewing is not permitted at school.

7.Buying, selling, or trading personal items such as candy, gum, toys, or similar items is not allowed on school
grounds or at school events.
8.Students are expected to keep school property and learning spaces clean and in good condition. Vandalism or
intentional damage to school property is not permitted.
9.Students must remain in supervised areas at all times and are not permitted to wander the building or campus
without permission.
10.Respectful behavior is expected toward all staff, volunteers, parish members, and peers. Disrespect, defiance,
or uncooperative behavior—including refusal to follow directions, arguing, or inappropriate language—is not
acceptable.
11.Physical aggression, including hitting, kicking, punching, or any behavior intended to harm others, is not
permitted.
12.Students are expected to represent St. Martha School appropriately in all forms of communication and online
activity. The use of school names, logos, images of staff, or school property without permission is not allowed.
Students must also follow age requirements for social media platforms.
13.Threats of violence in any form—verbal, written, or electronic—are taken very seriously. Any such behavior
will result in immediate investigation and may involve a formal safety response and law enforcement
notification.

Lunchroom Expectations

1.Students are expected to be respectful, responsible, and courteous in the lunchroom at all times, including
following directions from staff and volunteers and treating others with kindness.

2.Students will enter, line up, remain seated, and exit the lunchroom in an orderly manner. Cutting in line, loud
behavior, horseplay, or disruption of others is not permitted.
3.Students will remain seated with their class until dismissed by school staff.
4.Students are responsible for cleaning up after themselves by returning trays and disposing of trash properly.
5.Microwaves may be used appropriately for warming leftovers only, following school guidelines.

Recess/Playground Expectations
1.Students will treat one another and all supervisors with respect, kindness, and cooperation at all times.
2.Students are expected to play safely and fairly. Rough play, fighting, tackling, or any activity that could cause
harm is not allowed.
3.Playground equipment must be used properly and respectfully. Vandalism, misuse, or damage of any kind is
not permitted.
4.Students must remain within designated playground boundaries and go directly to the playground area at
recess.
5.Students will use appropriate language and behavior at all times. Disrespect toward supervisors, including
refusal to follow directions, arguing, shouting, or defiance, is not permitted.
6.At the end of recess, students will stop play immediately at the whistle, collect and put away equipment, and
line up at their designated spot in an orderly manner.

Restorative Justice

Conflicts and behavioral concerns will first be addressed through a restorative approach that focuses on repairing
harm and rebuilding relationships. Rooted in empathy, respect, and accountability, this process helps students
understand the impact of their actions, take responsibility, and actively participate in making things right. The goal
is to build community and strengthen relationships while supporting reflection, communication, and problem-
solving skills among students and staff.

When appropriate, all involved parties may take part in respectful dialogue to better understand what happened and
work toward resolution. This approach promotes shared understanding and helps foster a school culture grounded
in care, respect, and responsibility. When necessary, logical consequences will also be applied to support learning
and growth.

Consequences

Disrespectful, destructive, or inappropriate behavior will be addressed in a manner that supports student growth
and accountability. When a student is not meeting expectations for conduct, the school will respond based on the
nature, frequency, and severity of the behavior.

Responses may include, as appropriate:
Teacher-student conference
Logical consequences related to the behavior
Communication with parents (phone call, email, or note)
Apology or restorative action toward those impacted
Behavior plan or reflection process
Loss of recess or privileges
Silent lunch or lunch detention
School service or cleanup duty
Principal Discipline Notice
Parent conference
Exclusion from school activities or field trips
Early dismissal or being sent home
Probation, suspension, or expulsion when necessary
Faculty and staff will only discuss information related to your own child. Information regarding other
students will not be shared. If a parent is unwilling to support or allow appropriate consequences for a
student’s behavior, a meeting with administration (and the pastor when necessary) will be required.

title: Major behavior response rubric
content:
St. Martha School is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and Christ-centered learning environment where every student is treated with dignity. Behaviors that compromise the safety, well-being, or dignity of others including physical aggression, unsafe physical contact, and discriminatory or offensive language are inconsistent with our Catholic values and will be addressed promptly.

Whenever appropriate, restorative practices and logical consequences will be used to promote reflection, accountability, and the repair of relationships. The principal reserves the right to determine appropriate disciplinary action based on the severity of the behavior, the student's age and developmental level, prior behavior, intent, and the safety of the school community.

The following behaviors significantly impact the safety, dignity, or well-being of others and require administrative involvement.

Examples include, but are not limited to:

• Severe physical aggression (hitting, punching, kicking, fighting, or intentional physical harm)
• Rough play or unsafe physical contact (play fighting, wrestling, pushing, body checking, or other unsafe physical interactions)
• Discriminatory, offensive, or abusive language, including racial or ethnic slurs, derogatory remarks, swearing directed at others, or language that demeans another person's identity or dignity.

Major Behavior Response Rubric

1st Occurrence

Teacher implements an appropriate logical consequence, reteaches expectations, documents the behavior, and communicates with parents. Administration may be involved depending on the severity of the incident.

Repeated Behavior

Principal discipline notice, parent contact, restorative conference, and appropriate school consequences, which may include loss of privileges, behavior plan, detention, or suspension.

Continued or Severe Behavior

Administrative intervention with parent conference. Consequences may include in-school suspension, out-of-school suspension, behavior contract, or other disciplinary action deemed appropriate by the principal. Law enforcement may be contacted when required by law or when safety is compromised.

Please Note: The principal reserves the right to bypass progressive discipline when a student's behavior poses a significant safety risk, involves serious aggression, threats, harassment, discriminatory conduct, or any action that substantially disrupts the learning environment. Consequences will be determined based on the severity of the incident, the student's age and developmental level, intent, prior behavior, and the safety of the school community.

title: Communication channels
content:
FACTS Family Portal

The FACTS Family Portal is St. Martha School’s primary communication and information system for families. Once registered, families will receive an email with login credentials and instructions for access. Families are encouraged to securely save their username and password for ongoing use.

The portal is used to view grades and general school information, access report cards, manage tuition and other payments (including lunch and incidental charges), complete re-enrollment, add and track volunteer hours, and manage school lunch accounts.

News Notes

The weekly newsletter is emailed to parents every Tuesday and serves as an important source of school communication. Unless there is an unforeseen circumstance, Tuesday News Notes will be sent consistently each week. Families are encouraged to read it regularly to stay informed about school events, updates, and important information.

Email

Teachers and staff will make every effort to respond to parent emails within 24 hours during the school week. This expectation does not include weekends, holidays, or school breaks. Emails received on Fridays or before a holiday will be responded to on the next school day.

Cell Phone & Texting

In keeping with the “family atmosphere” of St. Martha School, some teachers and staff may choose to share their personal cell phone numbers, though this is not required. Families are asked to use discretion when contacting staff in this way, as teachers are actively engaged with students during the school day. For all school-related messages or time-sensitive communication, parents are encouraged to contact the school office directly, as staff may not be able to check email or messages until the end of the school day.

ClassDojo (PreK-4)

ClassDojo is a communication tool used to keep families connected to what is happening in the classroom through updates, messages, and occasional photos or reminders. Each teacher may use it a little differently depending on the needs of their classroom. Parents are encouraged to view themselves as partners in their child’s learning and to check ClassDojo regularly to stay informed and support classroom expectations at home.

Requested Teacher & Principal Meetings

To ensure staff availability and minimize disruptions to the school day, parents are asked not to drop in for meetings. Parents who wish to meet with the principal or any staff member should call or email the school to schedule an appointment in advance.

title: Copyright & technology acceptable use
content:
Copyright is a form of protection provided under the laws of the United States (Title 17, U.S. Code) to the authors
of “original works of authorship,” including literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, and other intellectual works. This
protection applies to both published and unpublished works.

Section 106 of the 1976 Copyright Act generally grants the owner of a copyright the exclusive right to do and to
authorize others to do the following:
Reproduce the work in copies or phonorecords
Prepare derivative works based upon the original work
Distribute copies or phonorecords of the work to the public through sale, transfer of ownership, rental, lease,
or lending
Perform the work publicly in the case of literary, musical, dramatic, choreographic, motion picture, and other
audiovisual works
Display the work publicly in the case of literary, musical, dramatic, choreographic, pictorial, graphic, or
sculptural works, including individual images from motion pictures or other audiovisual works
In the case of sound recordings, perform the work publicly by means of digital audio transmission
In addition, certain authors of visual works are granted rights of attribution and integrity under Section 106A of the
1976 Copyright Act. For further information, individuals may request Circular 40, Copyright Registration for
Works of the Visual Arts.

It is illegal to violate any of the rights provided to copyright owners. However, these rights are not unlimited.
Sections 107 through 121 of the Copyright Act establish important limitations, including exemptions from liability
in certain cases.

One major limitation is the doctrine of “fair use,” outlined in Section 107, which allows limited use of copyrighted
material without permission under specific circumstances. In other cases, uses may be permitted through
compulsory licensing arrangements, which require payment of royalties and compliance with statutory conditions.
For additional information regarding copyright limitations, individuals should consult the Copyright Act or contact
the U.S. Copyright Office.

NOTE: Sound recordings are defined as works resulting from the fixation of a series of musical, spoken, or other
sounds, excluding those accompanying audiovisual works. Common examples include music, drama, or lecture
recordings. A sound recording is not the same as a phonorecord. A phonorecord refers to the physical medium in
which a work is stored, such as cassette tapes, CDs, vinyl records, or other formats.

title: Parent & student handbook acknowledgment
content:
Commitment to a Safe and Respectful School Community

St. Martha School is committed to fostering a safe, respectful, and supportive learning environment for all students. A student's behavior, whether it occurs on or off the school campus, may impact the safety and well-being of the individual student, other students, or the broader school community. Such behavior may also indicate concerns that require the school's attention and support.

As a Catholic learning community, St. Martha School partners with parents, students, administration, faculty, and staff to help young people grow into responsible, moral, and faith-filled individuals. In support of this shared mission, and notwithstanding any other provision of this handbook, parents and legal guardians acknowledge that the school's Code of Conduct and disciplinary policies may be applied to student behavior occurring both on and off school property when such behavior affects the safety, reputation, or well-being of the school community.
